Decision: Does TAB 4 take ownership of the Calendar module from the feature-module team?
CurrentEvidence: Calendar was built under the parallel feature-module conventions (co-located interface+impl, bilingual literals, one controller per module) — different from the Tasks/TM conventions.
Options: (a) full handover to TAB 4; (b) TAB 4 integrates only, the feature team keeps the module; (c) split — entity stays theirs, integration surface is TAB 4's
Recommendation: (a) full handover. Calendar synchronisation, recurrence and task linkage are all TAB 4 scope, and split ownership of one 131-line service would cost more to coordinate than to own.
Consequence: TAB 4 inherits the convention mismatch and must decide whether to normalise the strings to Resources.

Decision: How does Calendar reach the Workspace, now that the shell exists and already consumes ITaskService?
CurrentEvidence: A Workspace shell was created by another tab DURING this increment (BL/Workspace/*, Controllers/WorkspaceController.cs, 2026-08-06 10:30). It injects ITaskService for My Work but NOT ICalendarService, and has no agenda panel.
Options: (a) TAB 4 exposes ICalendarService/agenda methods and the shell author calls them, mirroring the Tasks pattern; (b) TAB 4 implements a workspace source interface the shell discovers; (c) the shell queries CalendarEvents directly
Recommendation: (a) — it is exactly the pattern already working for Tasks, needs no new abstraction, and keeps the calendar visibility rule (owner/company/attendee) inside CalendarService where it already is.
Consequence: (c) must be refused: it would re-implement the visibility rule in a second place and drift from CalendarService.Visible().

Decision: What is the time model for Tasks and Calendar?
CurrentEvidence: Calendar writes DateTime.Now and emits ISO without an offset; Tasks writes CreatedAt in UTC and DueDate as a bare local value.
Options: (a) store UTC everywhere + render in the user's zone; (b) store local + a named zone per event; (c) keep as-is for single-zone companies
Recommendation: (a) UTC + a company/user zone for rendering. (c) is only honest while every company is single-zone, and it is the assumption that breaks silently.
Consequence: A migration of existing rows is required, and it must be measured before it is run.

Decision: One-way publish or two-way external calendar sync?
CurrentEvidence: No sync of any kind exists.
Options: (a) ICS feed (read-only publish); (b) one-way push to Exchange/Google; (c) two-way sync with conflict resolution
Recommendation: (a) first — an authenticated ICS feed is small, reversible and covers most of the value. (c) is a project, not a feature, and needs a conflict policy before any code.
Consequence: (c) would make an external system a writer into CrossBusiness data — a boundary decision, not a technical one.

Decision: Does a task's due date become a calendar event, or a calendar VIEW over tasks?
Options: (a) materialise a CalendarEvent per task due date; (b) a read-only calendar view that unions tasks and events; (c) both, with the materialised event owned by the task
Recommendation: (b) a union VIEW. Materialising duplicates state and creates a second thing to keep in step — the defect class this tab has already had to remediate twice.
Consequence: (b) means the calendar surface reads from two sources and must not let a user 'drag' a task due date unless the task itself is updated.
